title: Ephemeral runtime auth token → alternative client without token
trigger: A service requires an ephemeral, single-use auth token that can only be generated from its runtime context (browser player, native app), blocking out-of-context fetches
principle: When a service requires an ephemeral auth token (single-use, short-lived, only generatable from the service's runtime context), you cannot fetch it out-of-context (extension SW, server, headless). Instead of trying to obtain the token (ephemeral = not reusable), use an alternative client/context that the service does not require that token for. Services often expose multiple client types (WEB, ANDROID, IOS, TV) with different auth requirements — the less-protected client (mobile/TV) usually skips the token requirement.

cases.context: YouTube WEB InnerTube client requires a PO Token (ephemeral, single-use, only available from the player runtime) for caption tracks; fetching from an extension returns empty bodies and all tracks get filtered out

applyFor: YouTube InnerTube API (WEB requires PO Token, ANDROID/IOS do not)
Google APIs with multiple client contexts (WEB vs MOBILE vs TV)
Any service with ephemeral runtime-only auth (anti-bot token, session token from player/app)
Scraping protected APIs — try an alternative client type before attempting to reverse-engineer token generation
